name: Nessa's Collection
summary: At Rut'theran Village, fish bones and scales gathered from nearby waters are prepared for study by Laird in Auberdine. Nessa's Collection shows the great size of aquatic life around Teldrassil's roots.

sections.title: Bounty of the World Tree
sections.body: Nessa Shadowsong lives in Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base, where she gathered fish bones and scales to compare island sea life with that of mainland Kalimdor. Catches from the waters around the Great Tree grow to striking size. Nessa sent physical proof across the sea to Laird, a fish merchant along Auberdine's docks. The parcel travels through Vesprystus, Rut'theran's hippogryph master, and offers practical evidence of Teldrassil's growing vitality.

sections.title: A Curious Comparison
sections.body: In Darkshore, Laird finds that the specimens far outsize their mainland counterparts. The collection holds jawbones nearly twice the size of those from fish native to the Darkshore coast, and scales as large as a clenched fist. For coastal night elves, the package offers a clear look at how greatly the waters around Teldrassil differ from northern Kalimdor's somber shores.

faq.answer: The collection holds fish bones and scales, including jawbones nearly twice the size of those from fish native to the Darkshore coast and scales as large as a clenched fist. The fish were caught in the waters around Rut'theran Village.

faq.q: Who is the collection being sent to?
faq.answer: Nessa sends the collection to Laird, a night elf fish vendor working along Auberdine's docks in Darkshore.

faq.q: Why did Nessa gather these fish specimens?
faq.answer: Nessa gathered the specimens to compare the large fish thriving around Teldrassil with marine life on mainland Kalimdor.

faq.q: How does the collection reach Auberdine?
faq.answer: You carry the package to Vesprystus, Rut'theran's hippogryph master, who arranges its passage across the water to Auberdine for delivery to Laird.

angles.text: As a night elf, you can see through the collection how the waters around Teldrassil differ from those of the mainland.
